data.name: Nirmay
data.gender_notes: Nirmay is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Nirmay refers to the creator or maker in Hindu mythology. It is derived from the Sanskrit word 'nir' meaning 'without' and 'may' meaning 'form'. This name is given to a child believed to have the potential to create or bring about positive changes. The name Nirmay carries the meaning “Creator, Maker” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Nirmay usually hope their child will grow to embody creator, maker and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: In Hinduism, Nirmay symbolizes the divine power within each individual to create their own destiny.
data.etymology: Nirmay belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Creator, Maker.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nirmay total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name Nirmay holds a great significance in Hindu culture. In ancient times, it was believed that each child is gifted with unique qualities and abilities. Nirmay is given to a child who is expected to manifest these traits and create positive impacts in the world. This name embodies the spirit of creation and innovation.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Nirmay represents the divine power bestowed upon an individual to bring about transformation in themselves and the world around them. It is a reminder of the profound potential within each one of us to make a difference and contribute to the greater good. By invoking the name Nirmay, we are encouraged to harness our inner creative force and strive for positive transformation.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Nirmay signifies "pure creation" or "manifestation in its purest form." It represents the belief in the inherent purity of the universe and the divine nature of all creation.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that The name Nirmay is mentioned in the Mahabharata as a region in ancient India. The name Nirmay carried significant spiritual weight in that era.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Nirmay remains relevant in modern Hindu society, representing a bridge between traditional Vedic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Hindu names.

name_in_real_life.story: Anita Nirmay from Bali, Indonesia embodies the meaning of Nirmay - "Creator, Maker". Growing up in a Hindu family, they were taught to honor the spiritual significance of their name and live according to dharma.
